_why: Where a burned caption line may NOT break, beyond word boundaries: inside a NUMBER, read the way it is said. Intl.Segmenter (ICU) cuts Chinese and Japanese numerals into pieces — 负|四, 四百|五十, 两|万|八千|八百 — and a validation film (2026-10-31) burned 「负 / 四」 and 「四百 / 五十」. One definition, read by both tiers: remotion/src/captionBreak.ts (glueSpans) and scripts/caption_words.py (glue_spans); tests/test_caption_words.py holds them to the same answers. A number span is: an optional PREFIX, a run of NUMERALS in which a JOINER may sit between two numerals, and a UNIT (one space allowed before it: 28,800 拍, 3.8 kg), plus a second one after an APPROXIMATOR (三十多岁, 十几天). Nothing inside the span is a break; its edges are untouched (the segmenter decides those).
